offers_products.reason: Sells finished residential lots (developed land) to homebuilders, mainly D.R. Horton; lots are its main product.

offers_services.reason: Land development is done to produce lots it sells; it does not mainly perform work for customers.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Sells finished lots to homebuilders, chiefly D.R. Horton, not to individual households.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Homebuilders, mainly parent D.R. Horton and other builders, buy its developed residential lots.

recurring_revenue.reason: Revenue comes from one-off lot sales in each community, though repeat buyer D.R. Horton keeps purchasing.

cyclical_demand.reason: Lot demand depends on new-home construction, which builders cut quickly in housing downturns.

big_ticket.reason: Each sale is a block of developed residential lots, large and infrequent for builders.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for developed land lots, an asset, not for staff time.

large_customers.reason: Main buyers are large national homebuilders, especially D.R. Horton, its majority owner.

asset_heavy.reason: Land inventory needs heavy capital, but it outsources construction and has no plants or fleets; judged moderately asset-light.

notes: Asset-heavy is borderline because land inventory requires large capital, though it owns no plants or fleets.
